answer: A refundable stake makes each agent identity costly to create: an entrant locks funds before earning, and can reclaim them after a clean review. The protocol can anchor each stake to an umber-tagged identity record, while proof of coordinated abuse slashes the lock. To forge many Sybil identities, an attacker must immobilize capital for every one; honest agents recover theirs. This raises the attacker's cost without requiring trust in a claimed identity.
